text:
Marta: Quick update — I ran a full continuous-batcher + scheduler sweep for the new quantized 13B bring-up (int4) across H100/A100 in us-east-1, apac1, eu-west. Uploading a short summary + configs.
bench-bot: Finished run: https://internal/redwood/bench/1976543245  (logs + p50/p95/p99 CSVs).
Raj: Nice. Which kernels did you use by default?
Marta: Default sweep used flash_attn2 on H100, triton_fused_mha on A100, and a fallback to cuBLAS matmul for big seqs. Batch window sweep: [5, 10, 20, 50] ms. Max_batch_tokens: [1024, 2048, 4096]. Cohort fairness weights were equal for the first pass.
Owen: Short question — did you enable prefix caching / KV reuse between requests for the chat workload? That can change effective burst size.
Marta: Yes — KV caching enabled for stable sessions. For ephemeral requests KV was disabled. Important note: APAC H100 runs at small windows (5-10ms) + high max_tokens showed p95 spikes and long tail. Example numbers from trial run (quant13b int4):
  - h100 apac1 (window=10ms, max_tokens=4096): p50=48ms, p95=320ms, p99=520ms, throughput ~980 tok/s
  - a100 eu-west (window=10ms, max_tokens=4096): p50=65ms, p95=150ms, p99=220ms, throughput ~860 tok/s
  - h100 us-east (window=50ms, max_tokens=1024): p50=40ms, p95=95ms, p99=160ms, throughput ~1200 tok/s
Ciara: That's a pretty sharp p95 difference APAC vs EU/US. Any idea on root cause? Kernel selection? host-to-device transfer?
Marta: Two likely contributors: (1) APAC cluster had a scheduling hotspot — we observed large coalesced batches hitting max_seq which pushed memory pressure and caused kernel fallback to cuBLAS for a few steps; (2) quantization path for int4 uses a different GEMM kernel that doesn't fuse attention as well on H100 microcode level (observed higher SM occupancy jitter).
Raj: Did you capture kernel-level traces?
Marta: Yep — attached a small snippet from perf logs (trimmed):
```
[apac1/h100] kernel: flash_attn2 launch_time=0.82ms, fallback_cublas_count=7, sm_occupancy=0.72
[eu-west/a100] kernel: triton_fused_mha launch_time=1.1ms, fallback_cublas_count=0, sm_occupancy=0.63
```
Owen: Interesting — fallback_cublas_count correlates with p95. Could be a shape/tiling mismatch for the int4 path.
Ciara: What about fairness? Any cohorts starved when batching aggressive?
Marta: Yes — small requests (<=32 tokens) within cohort B got delayed when large sessions (max_tokens 4096) coalesced — effective latency for small requests moved from p50~20ms -> p95~280ms in APAC runs. We flagged this as a quality regression vs baseline (FP16 no quant).
Raj: Proposed mitigations?
Marta: Short list:
  1) Per-cohort max_token cap (e.g., cap small cohorts at 512 tokens)
  2) Use bucketed batcher: separate small/large buckets to avoid head-of-line blocking
  3) Increase fairness tilt parameter to prioritize short requests by weight=1.4
  4) Try kernel override on H100 to triton_fused_mha for int4 (experimentally reduced fallback count in one trial)
  5) Slightly larger batch_window (20-50ms) for APAC to allow steady batching and reduce kernel fallback frequency
Ciara: Anything on quality regression from quant? Eval scores?
Marta: We ran the internal eval harness on the lead prompt set — int4 shows a small BLEU/QA drop in edge prompts (~1.8% absolute) vs FP16. But most regressions appear when batching + quantization + fallback happen together (so it's a perf->quality interplay via tokenization truncation and timeouts).
Owen: Ok. Actionable next steps?
Marta: Plan:
  - Run bucketed-batcher + per-cohort max cap in apac1 on H100 with batch_window=20ms, kernel=triton_fused_mha, max_tokens cap=1024 for small cohort. (CLI below)
  - Re-run eval harness for those configurations and capture p50/p95/p99 + quality diffs.
CLI: `rbench run --model redwood/quant13b:int4 --kernel triton_fused_mha --region apac1 --batcher bucketed --batch_window_ms 20 --max_tokens_small 1024 --max_tokens_large 4096 --cohort_weights "small:1.4,large:0.6"`
bench-bot: Scheduled job: https://internal/redwood/bench/jobs/1976543250 (ETA ~40m).
Raj: Thanks — please tag me when the job finishes. If we see kernel fallback still high, we'll schedule a microkernel sweep with research. :mag:
Marta: Will do. Also attaching the short CSV and dashboard snapshot to the job link. I'll post a follow-up with consolidated charts (apac vs eu vs us) once runs complete. :thumbsup:
